title: Cancellation of a supplied unit pivot preserves an augmented bounded free resolution
statement: Let R be a nontrivial commutative ring, M an R-module and P a projective resolution of M [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], zero above d. Suppose bases b_i indexed by Fin(n_i) are supplied in every natural degree [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Fix j<d and source and target pivot indices p in Fin(n_(j+1)) and q in Fin(n_j), and suppose the (q,p) matrix coefficient of the differential P_(j+1) to P_j is a unit. There exists a projective resolution P′ of M with finite free terms [def-weil-finitely-generated-module; def-weil-pbc-free-module], zero above d, whose finrank is at most that of P at every degree in Fin(d+1) and strictly smaller at j. No local-ring assumption, nonminimality criterion or existential choice of a pivot is included.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00MT; augmentation preservation used in Tag 00OA. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00MT and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OA.

proof.text: Extend by zero to integer degrees, including empty bases in negative degrees. Apply ChainComplex.exists_splitting_of_isUnit_entry to the supplied unit coefficient in degree j+1. Restrict the complementary complex to natural degrees. Its basis sizes decrease by one at j and j+1 and agree elsewhere.

The removed two-term identity complex is contractible: use the inverse differential as the only nonzero component of the contracting homotopy. Its augmentation is zero, since at j=0 its degree-zero term is a differential image and for j>0 its degree-zero term is zero. Restrict the original augmentation to the complement. Homology of a binary direct sum splits, so inclusion of the complement induces homology isomorphisms. Composing with the original quasi-isomorphic augmentation gives a quasi-isomorphism to M in degree zero. Finite free terms are projective; with the restricted augmentation these data form a ProjectiveResolution M.

The complement above d is a direct summand of a zero term and hence zero. Nontrivial commutative rings have invariant basis number. Identify finite basis sizes with finrank; the splitting gives nonincrease at every degree and a drop by one at j.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_bounded_resolution_unit_entry_cancellation {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Nontrivial R] (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (d : ℕ) (P : ProjectiveResolution M)
    (hzero : ∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (P.complex.X i))
    (n : ℕ → ℕ) (b : ∀ i : ℕ, Module.Basis (Fin (n i)) R (P.complex.X i))
    (j : ℕ) (hjd : j < d) (p : Fin (n (j + 1))) (q : Fin (n j))
    (hu : IsUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix (b (j + 1)) (b j)
      (P.complex.d (j + 1) j).hom q p)) :
    ∃ P' : ProjectiveResolution M,
      (∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (P'.complex.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite R (P'.complex.X i) ∧ Module.Free R (P'.complex.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), Module.finrank R (P'.complex.X i.val) ≤
        Module.finrank R (P.complex.X i.val)) ∧
      Module.finrank R (P'.complex.X j) < Module.finrank R (P.complex.X j)
